Mar 11, 2015 16:37:14 GMT -5 DirtyDivisions said:
I'm so happy you and Jonathan Mejia worked so hard to make this the best forum on the Internet dealing with Sarracenia.  I have tried other forums and they don't even come close to having the resources, information, and community that The Sarracenia Forum offers. The members of this forum have become a part of my family. I love you all!

Thanks for the warm sentiment. I think it is more the other members. As a matter of fact, most of the things I try out on the forum don't succeed.

Like the history of the forum via monthly updates:
Feb 2014 update , March 2014 update, April 2014 update

I am a huge nerd, and so this stuff interests me. However the very few responses I got to these posts, coupled with the amount of time and resources it took to compile them wasn't worth it. There were some times I tried to make more resources available on the forum, and it didn't work well. Most of the most useful resources were posted by our members. So thank all of you for making this place amazing!

Mar 11, 2015 16:55:12 GMT -5 dozer1028 said:
Fantastic Mike and Jonathan. . I'm glad to be a part of this forum family. This forum is a great community of people and it's getting better everyday. Thanks guys...


I agree. The growth is very often cyclical, where most people join as Sarracenia break out of dormancy, and the forums become very active again! I hope the growth of our family and its community continues, as the more people we have, the more resources available, and the better the forum can become.

Mar 11, 2015 19:18:43 GMT -5 calen said:
meizzwang and Jonathan Mejia
I second what Mike said: Jonathan you not only created the forum but continue to be a fantastic administrator and contributor, soliciting feedback and pushing the limits of what people typically think a "mere forum" can do. You take responsibility but are not proprietary - a true community organizer. Thank you JM!!!
Mike: ... You have absolutely set the tone for the forum and been the example of how to treat others in this arena. If you had been a total wang (lower case w), like some on the interwebs, no way we would be here!
A great thread for a great community. Thanks to everyone who contributes - we have a pretty sweet thing going.



calen You haven't seen anything yet concerning pushing limits on what a 'mere forum' can do. I am trying to build something big here, but I don't want to give up ALL the playing cards before they are ready. Besides, these ideas, if they come to fruition will be very big, and will involve a number of projects... should I give hints about some of the ideas? How we publish a book on Sarracenia's? Or a Sarracenia Forum Year in Review Video/Youtube Channel? How about advocate for Mike and Rob Co to be on Sci Show (the biggest science youtube channel?) or on Ellen? What if we were more proactive IRL?
For example, when sflynn wrote about finding the yellow flowered leucophylla in the wild, and about contacting the Atlanta Botanical Gardens about preserving the genetics, or even the site. What if I was more proactive, and wrote my own letter to them, and then goodkoalie and greenbeast, and meizzwang, and philcula, and brie, and davidgreen and rhizomatous also wrote letters? Do you think they will ignore a hoard of people the same way they haven't responded to sflynn ?

However in what order to release, and how we should go about the group projects is still in the back burner. I have these plus MANY MANY MANY MANY other ideas in a huge text file. Currently they are in the stages of being brought out one by one, and they include IRL community outreach, spreading our love of Sarracenia into other forms of media/to get attention/build a platform. Once that platform is built, and the educational part of the project give a steady stream of info to the public, we can start to focus as a group on getting legislation passed that protects Sarracenia in a similar way that Dionaea are protected in the wild (with harsh penalties for their removal/harsh penalties for destruction of their habitats. Other projects include maintaining the genetic diversity of these plants, and making this diversity available in the form of seeds to people who want them (be them scientists or people on the forum via free giveaways). My interest is not to ever make money. Just to forward the sarracenia cause, and many of the projects, currently in the contemplative stage, need to be better thought out, but they generally deal with these themes: Legislation, Education, Outreach, Popular Media/Growing Our Community, Making Resources available to everyone.

I am hesitant about making large claims about what we will do though. Everything is still contemplative. Just like in Christmas Carol, we need to think of these ideas not as things that will come to pass, but as things which might come to pass. Because there is still the real possibility that drama will come and drastically change our forum. There is still a real possibility that we wont get legislation though, and even though we care, habitats will still be destroyed at an anxiety inducing rate. One of the saddest realities is that the impetus lies on the people who care to do something. That is us!

As for being a Community Organizer, funny story...
In 2008 I was still in college, and as part of the ALANA (Asian/Latin/African/Native American) Student center, I won an award. The award was given to one student every year who has done exceptional community building.
And here I am with the plaque the gave me:

yne last note, you are absolutely right about Mike setting the stage for how people interact on the forums. His generosity of information, and fairness, and the amount of time he has given, has set a tone that if you care about this, you spend time here, and you treat people with kindness and respect. Even small things like giving people an extra plant or two with their order, or helping sort out complex histories where discrepancies occur, have been done in a way that are drama free, and I really hope the atmosphere of friendliness and genuine respect live on. It's like Mike said, it doesn't matter if you are a celebrity here or not. Everyone is treated with respect and kindness, and no one is ignored.

Mar 11, 2015 23:03:35 GMT -5 billredlionpa said:
This forum does have a great community and I love the atmosphere here! meizzwang Jonathan Mejia you guys have done a lot for Sarracenias by founding this forum. Appreciation for the hobby is definitely on the upswing! One indicator would be the recent great results philcula has had with his auctions.


I sure hope you are correct that we have done a lot by founding the forum. I mean, I love that we all have a safe friendly place to hang out and talk online, and that we have met new people. I actually hope on meeting with greenbeast and midtowncarnivores more this year at reptile expos and events at botanical gardens and such. But I wonder if our efforts might be more influential elsewhere. Perhaps we need to shine a light on other places of import, like detecting, and bringing to people attention, potentially new populations. Or perhaps our efforts should be given the growing our community in our local neighborhoods via outreach. Sarracenia NW does an excellent job with their weekly presence at the Portland Saturday Market, and midtowncarnivores has an excellent education and outreach program I hope others can emulate. As a matter of fact I will be there too to talk to Jonathan (from midtown carnivores, not myself, that would be weird), and learn more about it.

I hope we can grow in terms of numbers and interest, but also in terms of effectiveness, and actually "doing something". There is so much awesomeness here. If we think impossibly big, we can achieve big things.

]okay seriously, I almost wanted to do a compilation of all the action memes!!! I really love this forum. People are super helpful, nice, and funny. Thanks to the creator of this forum and all the other content contributors. Salute to you guys!

Compilation of Memes on the forum huh? Give me two days.

Mar 12, 2015 10:23:25 GMT -5 billredlionpa said:
Jonathan Mejia this is a fascinating account of the forum origins!  I've been looking for a place that I 'click' with for a while as well, and this hobby seems to attract people with a lot of attributes that I feel coincide with my own.  Congrats on getting it off the ground, and a big Thank You! to the early founders who posted back when it probably felt like a ghost town.


Ghost town was an understatement. Until Mike emailed me, I literally never checked the forums! It was dead even to me!
As for clicking, one great things about people in general is that, if you put people in a room, they quickly begin to build a culture. Either a culture of being quiet and not talking, or of sharing ideas, or of being silly. Whatever it is, culture is built when people get together. And culture is always unique. In south America, dancing is a major part of the culture. In America it is football and baseball, and reality TV. The culture on the forum seems to be one of respect, of giving (freebees, extras, giveaways), and where people who wants answers, can get them.

The culture of our community is what keeps people coming back. If people felt the forum was dry, they would just use it as an encyclopaedia. But they don't. But keeping our culture rich, with events, and projects, I hope to help grow our culture as well. Happy pi day btw.

Mar 12, 2015 11:22:11 GMT -5 meizzwang said:
Dude Jonathan, that was a freaking awesome story! Man, your nerdiness runs so deep, I gotta get on my hands and knees and bow to you, haha! You definitely out-nerd me on many levels, mad respect to dat! You do things behind the scenes that most of us benefit from but have no clue how it happens (ie. why we have only cool people on this forum, thank you David G. and Andrew G!!). Seriously, you're the mastermind behind this whole Forum, and I feel lucky that so many people here came together under your guidance and coalesced into this community we have today!

I had no IDEA that Rob DAWG was a part of the formation of this place!!!! Dude Rob, THANK YOU!!!!!!!!!!! Aside from his mad talent at growing, Rob Co is the master P.R. man, he's got skills like nobody else in that area!

I should be the one thanking you! Nerdiness is good for some things, like putting an instagram feed of constantly updated pictures on the bottom of the homepage, but bad for others, like making good interpersonal connections. I am actually quite introverted IRL, and so online communities are very appealing to me. However I do wish to break out of my shell, and have more than just two people I call close friends.

As for out-nerding, you don't know the half. I am a huge edgar allen poe/stephen king fan, and I have the complete collection of shakespeare, of which i read one or two plays/poems a year. I can solve a rubiks cube from any position in under two minutes. My video game collection just recently reached over 500 games.
backloggery.com/jmejia1187

I feel like my contributions, other than maintaining this forum, have been minimal. As for guidance, the community decided everything about the t-shirt, and greenthumb and goodkoalie were the masterminds behind the auction.

Most things I do on the forum do not end up going well. Like remember the newsletter that never took off?
drive.google.com/file/d/0B-NKSkcxA6mSM3NmZ3dNV2RhSDA/edit

Yeah, epic fail. I did wish we had more people interested in that sort of thing, but I had to let it go because my guidance had tried to introduce something to the forum that it wasn't ready, or willing to do. However there is a creative vision of the forum which I think helps guide us a bit.

Mar 12, 2015 11:48:30 GMT -5 ps3isawesome said:
Jonathan Mejia, Wow, thanks for sharing that story. I also love Dan Brown. I found him when he was uploading videos during his trips to China and his commentary was hilarious. Has subscribed ever since and you can say I am kind of part of his pogo tribe. His talent with the cube and pogo stick is hilarious!

I also think there's much more of a community sense here as well as Flytrapcare. People here are super duper nice and it feels like home.

AH ANOTHER POGOTRIBIAN LUNARIAN!
I love his video where he solves a rubiks cube on a pogostick!

His recent videos are very interesting as well, where people email him and he responds. Dan 3.0 was an epic fail, but his brief foray into generating a tribe of people who wanted to use their weirdness and awesomeness for good is the main reason we are all here today. I feel bad about the members of the forum revolting against and impeaching him. Somewhere inside, I always thought his impeachment was an inside job. Like, they did it because he wanted to let his tribe go and be self sufficient without his constant oversight. Being that the last post on the moon was in 2013, and that the moon was effectively an empty graveyard since 2011, it was evident that this was not the case.

I really hope this never happens to our little home. bombmaniac on the south pole of the moon was one of the last people to leave. When Dan tried to come back, he was very harsh on him, saying:
"You didn't create a forum; you created a movement. The majority of people who joined South Pole of the Moon joined because you offered a vision of change and progress. Of community building. So we waited. We waited through all your hemmings and hawings, through all your protracted ideas and failures, through all your successes and all your disasters. Why? Because we still had that common goal, that shared vision that we may someday accomplish something real and meaningful."

Many people made their own communities and branched off, like I did. When Dan left, everyone raised hell, because they felt abandoned. I really hope our forum is more than just a forum. I hope it has an atmosphere which does move people. But unlike Dan and the pogotribe, who wanted to accomplish something big (and never figured out what it was), we know what our goals are!
-Educating people about Sarracenia
-Preserving Wild Populations and ecosystems
-Maintaining a genetic library of Sarracenia via live specimens, and sharing those genetics with others via trade/giveaway/sales.
-Building a platform where we can build awareness of our causes to the general public.

There probably are other goals but these are a few of the main ones. And so we move on, remembering the ideals that worked, and throwing out those that didn't.

Mar 13, 2015 5:13:02 GMT -5 Jonathan Mejia said:
There is a bigger plan for this community, which I hope to share with you soon, and has a LOT to do with the recently made Group Projects section.

 Fingers crossed in hopes that your plans include a militant uprising.

Read my reply to calen earlier in this post. Does any of it sound like a militant uprising? If so, then that is what I am planning, HOWEVER it will be a volunteer militia, and an uprising of minds, not of guns.

The concerned parents will just have to understand. Besides, in NYC, the parent cuss more than the children do.

As for your daughter, first off, congratulations. Secondly, don't hide the real you from her too long. If you are as awesome IRL as you are here, then she should see who you really are, cusses and all.


Hope this answers everyones questions/replies to everyones comments. If I missed someone I am sorry. Let me know and I'll get back to you!

So we waited. We waited through all your hemmings and hawings, through all your protracted ideas and failures, through all your successes and all your disasters. Why? Because we still had that common goal, that shared vision that we may someday accomplish something real and meaningful."
Many people made their own communities and branched off, like I did. When Dan left, everyone raised hell, because they felt abandoned. I really hope our forum is more than just a forum. I hope it has an atmosphere which does move people. But unlike Dan and the pogotribe, who wanted to accomplish something big (and never figured out what it was), we know what our goals are!
-Educating people about Sarracenia
-Preserving Wild Populations and ecosystems
-Maintaining a genetic library of Sarracenia via live specimens, and sharing those genetics with others via trade/giveaway/sales.
-Building a platform where we can build awareness of our causes to the general public.
There probably are other goals but these are a few of the main ones. And so we move on, remembering the ideals that worked, and throwing out those that didn't.
